## Body

F211 (#253): a spawn answered ok:false yet left a live seat. Root cause was a daemon RESTART mid-wait (find it with daemon.log boot lines at the spine timestamp), not any handler step. My round 1 keyed the parent notice to one event order (bind sees "unreported"), and the reviewer broke it twice: bind-then-drop, and bind just before a timeout built from a stale row. The shape that holds: keep two INDEPENDENT facts per launch (bound / answered-with-the-seat). Whichever of "bound" and "not answered" comes second does the hand-off, exactly once. Settle only AFTER the answer is built, never before an await. For restarts, persist evidence (spawn.launched before the row, spawn.answered, spawn.reported). At boot, unsettled = launched with neither of the others, bound or NOT. Historical rows have no launched event, so they are never flagged. Quote printed commands with pij_core::directory::shell_word. Correlate by seat+pane, not just an id.

F209 (#249/#251): a negative cache (MISS_TTL) froze the PA's size read, because the PA cached "not found" as a completed read and only re-reads on activity. Any cache you add: check every consumer that caches its answer in turn, and make transient answers retryable there (NotFound -> stale). Incremental projections (all_matching_after on the (seat,kind,seq) index) beat full replays. A required port method means about 14 wrapper impls; delegate those mechanically.

F202 (#248): measure a launch rate with the daemon's uptime next to both readings. A boot burst looks like a steady rate in a 20 s window. Walk to .git from the CANONICAL path (a symlink places by its target) and read pointer files only if regular and <= 4 KiB.

Disk: tests build pij-rs into EACH worktree's own target/ (about 15 GB per lane, outside the shared target). After a lane merges, rm -rf <worktree>/target, or shared-build hits the 25 GiB floor. Never lower the floor yourself; ask the PM.
